title: Permutation in String
oneLinerQuestion: Check if one string contains a permutation of another string as a substring.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The Permutation in String problem asks whether string s2 contains a substring that is a permutation of string s1. A permutation of s1 is simply an anagram of s1: it must have the exact same length as s1 and identical character frequencies. Sorting every substring of length len(s1) inside s2 takes O((|s2| - |s1| + 1) * |s1| log |s1|). Instead, we can maintain a fixed-size sliding window of length len(s1) across s2. Using two fixed-size frequency arrays of size 26 (or hash maps), we count character frequencies for s1 and the initial prefix window of s2. As the window slides one character to the right, we update the frequency table in O(1) time by adding the incoming character and removing the outgoing character, checking for frequency equality at each step.

- Step 1: Length Validation Guard — Compare lengths: `if (s1.length > s2.length) return false`. A longer string cannot be a substring of a shorter string.

- Step 2: Frequency Buckets Initialization — Allocate two fixed-size integer arrays of length 26: `const s1Count = new Array(26).fill(0)` and `const s2Count = new Array(26).fill(0)`.

- Step 3: Initial Window Seeding — Populate the counts for all characters in `s1` and the initial prefix window of `s2` of length `s1.length`: for `i = 0` to `s1.length - 1`, increment `s1Count[s1.charCodeAt(i) - 97]++` and `s2Count[s2.charCodeAt(i) - 97]++`.

- Step 4: Initial Match Check — Check if the first window matches: compare all 26 entries between `s1Count` and `s2Count`. If identical, return `true` immediately.

- Step 5: Sliding Window Traversal & Incremental Updates — Iterate through `s2` from index `i = s1.length` to `s2.length - 1`. At each step, incorporate the incoming character: `s2Count[s2.charCodeAt(i) - 97]++`, and evict the outgoing character from the left boundary: `s2Count[s2.charCodeAt(i - s1.length) - 97]--`.

- Step 6: Equality Evaluation & Early Exit — After updating the window counts, compare `s1Count` and `s2Count` (checking 26 bucket values or maintaining a running count of matching characters). If all 26 indices match, a valid permutation exists; return `true`.

- Step 7: Termination & Negative Fallback — If the sliding window traverses the entirety of `s2` without encountering matching character distributions, return `false`.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(|s2|) where |s2| is the length of s2, since the window slides in linear time with O(26) or O(1) comparison overhead per step. Space Complexity: O(1) auxiliary space (bounded by 26 fixed character buckets for lowercase English letters).
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION checkInclusion(s1, s2):
    IF LENGTH(s1) > LENGTH(s2) THEN RETURN False
    c1 = FREQ_MAP(s1), c2 = EMPTY_MAP(), l = 0
    FOR r FROM 0 TO LENGTH(s2) - 1 DO:
        c2[s2[r]] = c2[s2[r]] + 1
        IF (r - l + 1) == LENGTH(s1) THEN:
            IF c1 == c2 THEN RETURN True
            c2[s2[l]] = c2[s2[l]] - 1
            IF c2[s2[l]] == 0 THEN DELETE c2[s2[l]]
            l = l + 1
        END IF
    END FOR
    RETURN False
END FUNCTION
